## The goal
PRAMS & STROLLERS is forecast 14.2% (PHP 93.8M) below budget. About 92% of that gap is lower volume, not price. Actuals so far are tracking the forecast (-0.9%), so this gap is real. The department is overbought: 12.4 weeks of cover including on-order stock against a 7.7-week target, and open-to-buy is PHP -111.7M. Two classes cause most of the overbuy:
- **Travel System:** 17.1 weeks of cover against a 6.1-week target. This class is already on a Decline strategy.
- **Double Stroller:** 20.7 weeks against a 9.6-week target.

You didn't give a GP target, so I haven't run a GP goal-seek. I built two DRAFT range cuts that release stock, one for each overbought class, both cutting the bottom 25% for H2.

## The options
| Option | Sales | GP | GP rate | Stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Travel System, cut bottom 25% (18 of 73 options) | PHP -14.9M | PHP -2.9M | +0.93pp | PHP -10.2M |
| Double Stroller, cut bottom 25% (21 of 87 options) | PHP -9.3M | PHP -2.4M | +1.07pp | PHP -9.9M |

Both cuts improve GP rate and release about PHP 10M of stock each, but they cost sales and GP. Neither cut gets either class back to its target cover.



## Recommendation
**I recommend the Double Stroller cut (SCN-5c974da4…).** It releases almost the same stock as the Travel System cut (PHP 9.9M vs PHP 10.2M) but loses less sales and GP. It also gives the bigger GP rate gain and drops only 1 new option, against 3 for Travel System.

Its key assumption is that 35% of demand from the dropped options moves to the ones you keep (the planning default). If less moves, the sales loss gets bigger.

The Travel System cut also fits that class's Decline strategy, so you could add it later.

## Next step
Both scenarios are DRAFTS in the sandbox. Compare them on the Scenario Planning page, then submit and approve the one you choose there. Only approval updates the forecast.

If you want to close the GP gap rather than release stock, give me a GP target in PHP. I'll run a goal-seek that costs a price and promo move and a range addition.
